text:
Cole Perfetti has spent years as the skilled Jet waiting for a bigger job. This season he got it: 17:53 a night, up from 15:37, and on the ice for 89% of Winnipeg's power-play time after half of it last season. Our numbers flag it as a breakout, and Sportsnaut framed him and Björck as Winnipeg's "glimpse of future."

The production is honest. He has 20 points in 26 games, half of them on the power play, with nine goals on 10.7 expected and a shooting percentage right at league average. His own chances are up to 1.38 expected goals per 60 from 1.08, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him taking the best kind of passes last season, across the slot or from behind the net. Nothing here is hot finishing.

The one thing to watch is the defense. Evolving-Hockey had him 95th percentile at taking chances away last season, but the Jets get only 49% of the 5v5 expected goals with him on the ice this year, even as they take 53% of the shot attempts. His minutes have dipped in recent games. Whether the job keeps growing is the question of his season.
headline: Cole Perfetti's role finally matches the talent
